name: Ascension Tether (Galápagos Orbital Elevator)
description: The first and only functioning space elevator on Earth. Anchored to the northern tip of Isla Isabela in the former Galápagos Archipelago, the Ascension Tether is a 104,000-kilometer carbon nanotube ribbon connecting the surface to a counterweight station in geostationary orbit. The Anchor Station is a 12-square-kilometer industrial complex built on the blasted foundation of what was once the most biodiverse island ecosystem on the planet. Four fusion reactors power the electromagnetic climber cars that carry 200 metric tons of cargo per week to orbit. Annual revenue exceeds Φ2.1 trillion. The surrounding ocean — formerly the Galápagos Marine Reserve — is a restricted naval zone patrolled by Meridian Orbital Dynamics security vessels. The water is warm, clear, and dead. The last wild giant tortoise was seen in 2203. Construction consumed 40% of Isla Isabela and rendered the remaining 60% ecologically lifeless. The elevator hums. You can feel it in your teeth.
